method: harness: deterministic simulation, one command per round, 10 ticks apart, 1800 rounds = 18 000 ticks, shared boot, one named outcome per row plus one policy row, three supply tables (regular, irregular 5-on/4-off, gap6 3-on/3-off)
criteria: A1-2v3 (g2 addendum) plus STRAT-003 distinct prices: the two live plans carry different prices at the same level (plain ladder + BRANCH_PRICE_OFFSET: speed +10, draw +0, buffer +0); the `priced` row buys under the power-line signal (throttled -> draw, else speed) with a cheapest-affordable fallback; leaders under MMG reported for the named three and for the live pair

gaps.criteria: A1-2v3 (g2 addendum): per-column minimum meaningful gap replaces the retired '>= 5 % relative OR >= 10 absolute' disjunction; absolute-only when the rival is exactly 0
gaps.bufferRule: buffer leads inputStallPct by >= 3 points over the best named rival under BOTH gap ladders (irregular 5-on/4-off and gap6 3-on/3-off) or the drop executes and the fork ships two plans (speed, draw)
gaps.inputStall: rows[].inputStallTicks = sum over machines of ticks not busy while store.scrap <= TUNING.reserveFloor; rows[].inputStallPct = inputStallTicks / tick, reported on the 0-100 points scale (x100), the same unit as starvedMax/starvedMean

autoExec.question: does buffer lead inputStallPct by >= 3 points over the best named rival under BOTH gap ladders?
autoExec.outcome: the drop executes: the fork ships two plans (speed, draw); negative result recorded, never re-scored
